correctness.rationale: For any one- to three-point support, the outermost aperiodic autocorrelation fixes endpoints. A distinct-gap middle point is fixed by a unique lag. At equal gaps, the real-linear equation controlling the middle coefficient is injective if endpoint magnitudes differ; at equal endpoint magnitudes its two fixed-radius preimages are precisely the original coefficient and reflected conjugate. This exhausts cases without computation. For all admissible nonzero real parameters with the second parameter away from the unit-modulus boundary, the displayed four-polynomial pair has matching coordinate magnitudes and identical full-torus intensities by the factorization in the proof; first/last coefficient asymmetry excludes both trivial associations. The included pure-standard-library rational program passed sixteen parameter examples and the exact integer witness. It is a supplemental check, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The minimum support size for a genuinely nontrivial Pauli ambiguity is an intrinsic and directly motivated exact invariant in discrete full-frequency phase retrieval. The theorem establishes the sharp border across *all* one-, two-, and three-point support geometries and provides a continuous family at the first permitted support size. This isolates where paired time/Fourier intensity data cease to be rigid; unlike a coefficient identity, it resolves a natural obstruction threshold highlighted by existing sparse nonuniqueness constructions, while leaving higher-support classifications and stability open.
